title: Nineteen Miles and One Dry Well
subtitle: 地理与地貌 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 地理与地貌（自然生态·地理与地貌）
meta: 主题语境：地理与地貌（自然生态·地理与地貌）　|　核心词汇：desert　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 desert 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 the guide ① crossed a desert that no caravan in the province would have attempted, and he said the crossing was the whole of the season. The ② desert, meaning the sand and not the emptiness, ran nineteen miles and stayed unmapped; a desert, he said, is the only thing in a journey that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ desert in that province had the same dry well at the middle of it, and the ④ desert at the end, meaning the one they kept for the winter road and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever crossed twice. A desert, his driver said, is nine parts water and one part somebody willing to cross; the guide said the crossing is the part that fills nineteen miles.

The geographer meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the desert was the whole of the region, meaning the wasteland and not the sand. The ⑥ desert, meaning the wasteland and not any of that, is the only thing in a region that everybody names and nobody farms; desert, she said, is either something you cross or the only word that means both a sand and a wasteland. She said the wasteland is the part they remember.

By 1955 the ⑦ desert had become a line in an atlas, and the atlas had become an argument about the dry well. The ⑧ desert of the whole thing, the guide wrote in May, was one province and nineteen miles of crossing; desert, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to cross. She said the crossing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ desert I remember is the one at the end, which was mapped in 1970 and is still described as the driest in the province. A ⑩ desert, the driver said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being crossed; every desert, she said, is a wasteland that has agreed to look like a sand. She said the wasteland was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 沙漠；荒漠（指那个省里横亘的那一片）
B. n. 沙漠（指那片沙地本身，与那片空寂相对）
C. 固定搭配：cross a desert 穿越一片沙漠
D. n. 沙漠（指留给冬季道路用的那一片）
E. n. 沙漠；荒漠（抽象总称，指一个省里的沙漠全貌）
F. n. 沙漠（指地图册上标出、被绘制的那一片）
G. n. 荒芜之地；不毛之地（指那个地区里无人耕种的土地）
H. n. 荒地（抽象总称，指人人叫得出名却无人耕种的那片）

items.q: crossed a desert that no caravan in the province would have attempted
The desert, meaning the sand and not the emptiness
the desert was the whole of the region
the desert had become a line in an atlas
The desert of the whole thing
A desert, the driver said in 1972

answers.why: cross a desert 意为“穿越一片沙漠”，1946 年向导穿越了一片全省没有一支商队敢尝试的沙漠。
desert 意为“沙漠”，指那片沙地本身而不是那片空寂，它长达十九英里而未被测绘。
desert 意为“沙漠”，指那个省里每一片沙漠，每一片中间都有同一口干井。
desert 意为“沙漠”，指留给冬季道路用的那一片，是唯一有人穿越过两次的。
desert 意为“荒芜之地、不毛之地”，指那个地区里无人耕种的土地，地理学家说这片荒地就是那个地区的全部。
desert 意为“荒地”，指人人叫得出名却无人耕种的那片而不是那片沙地，是地区里人人都叫得出名、却无人耕种的东西。
desert 意为“沙漠”，指地图册上标出、被绘制的那一片，到 1955 年这片沙漠成了地图册上的一行。
desert 意为“沙漠、荒漠”，向导五月写道，整件事的荒漠是一个省和十九英里的穿越。
desert 意为“沙漠”，我记得的是末尾那一片，1970 年被测绘，至今仍被说成全省最干的一片。
desert 为抽象总称，司机 1972 年说，一片沙漠是唯一会因为被穿越而变得更好的地方。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1946 年向导穿越了一片全省没有一支商队敢尝试的沙漠，他说穿越才是那个季节的全部。（cross a desert）
那片沙漠，指的是那片沙地本身而不是那片空寂，长达十九英里而未被测绘。（desert）
那个省里每一片沙漠中间都有同一口干井。（desert）
末尾那一片沙漠，指的是他们留给冬季道路用的那一片，是唯一有人穿越过两次的。（desert）
地理学家说这片荒地就是那个地区的全部，指的是那片不毛之地而不是那片沙地。（desert）
1972 年司机说，一片沙漠是唯一会因为被穿越而变得更好的地方。（desert）
